video.encoderDetectingHint: Running test encodes; the encoders available on this computer appear when done.
video.encoderAvailableHint: Only encoders that passed a test encode on this computer are shown.
video.proresHint: ProRes quantizer 1–64: lower means higher quality and larger files; 0 is the encoder default (measured at about 4× the size of quantizer 12). 4:2:2 maps to HQ, 4:4:4 to 4444.
video.bitrateHint: Target average bitrate (kbps): higher usually means better quality and larger files. With single-pass VBR the actual bitrate varies, so the file size is not guaranteed.
video.qpHint: Constant QP: lower means less compression. Complex scenes use the same quantizer, so quality and bitrate vary.
video.crfHint: CRF constant quality: lower means higher quality. Bitrate follows scene complexity; CRF values of different software encoders are not directly comparable.
video.cqHint: CQ target quality: the hardware allocates bitrate per scene; lower usually means higher quality. CQ and CRF use different scales.
video.speedProresHint: ProRes uses its profile to set compression.
video.speedNvencHint: p1 is fastest, p7 favours compression efficiency; actual speed depends on the GPU and processing chain.
video.speedAv1Hint: For AV1, lower numbers are slower and usually more efficient; higher numbers are faster.
video.speedAmfHint: speed favours speed, quality favours compression efficiency, balanced is in between.
video.speedCpuHint: veryfast / ultrafast are faster; slow / veryslow are slower and usually more efficient.
video.resizeLong: Scale by long edge · Detects landscape/portrait
video.longEdgeHint: Used as the width for landscape videos and the height for portrait ones; the other side keeps the original ratio.
video.sizeInteger: Enter a whole number from 2 to 16384
video.keepAspectHint: On by default; the other side follows each source video's ratio, rounded to the nearest even pixel.
video.keepAspectEmpty: The other side is calculated once videos are added.
video.fpsConversionHint: Lowering the frame rate keeps the duration and A/V sync; raising it repeats frames and adds no motion detail.
video.audioBitrateNoneHint: No audio, so no bitrate is needed.
video.audioBitrateLosslessHint: Lossless or uncompressed audio does not use a target bitrate.
video.audioBitrateHint: Target bitrate; the actual bitrate varies with the encoder and the sound.
video.audioFadeNoneHint: No audio, so no fade is needed.
video.hiRes: Hi-Res audio (24-bit; doubles the sample rate when below 48 kHz)
video.hiResDisabled: Available with FLAC or PCM audio.
video.hiResPerSource: Calculated from each video's own audio track.
video.audioHint: Keeps the source sample rate and channels; MP4 uses AAC, FLAC uses MKV. To use different audio, click ♪ in the queue to choose it for that video; it is cut to the video's length.
video.alphaSplit: Separate alpha · Color video + B/W mask
video.alphaSplitHint: The color video has no alpha and can use any encoder and container; a black-and-white mask with the same size and frame rate is exported alongside it (_alpha suffix, {format}). White is opaque, black is transparent, and grey keeps partial transparency.
video.alphaMaskHint: Exports only a black-and-white mask with the same size and frame rate (_alpha suffix, lossless, no audio), without the color video. WebM uses VP9, other formats H.264; the encoder settings on the Quality tab don't affect the mask. White is opaque, black is transparent, and grey keeps partial transparency.
video.alphaMissing: This source has no readable alpha channel, so no mask can be exported. Choose another option or a video with transparency.
video.outputHint: Your last choice is remembered. Each source folder gets its own Encoded folder.
video.nameTemplateHint: The extension is added automatically; duplicate names are numbered.
video.templateTokens: Original name / Preset name / Date / Queue number
video.outputExampleEmpty: The full path appears once videos are added
video.editFriendlyManual: A GOP interval is set manually, so this has no effect.
video.editFriendlyHint: The result can be cut losslessly at about 1-second intervals; files are about 2%–5% larger at the same quality (more with software encoders).
video.commandEmpty: The command is generated once videos are added
video.ownHint: When on, the settings below apply only to the selected video
video.autoSave: Settings save automatically · All pending videos share these settings
rtx.noResizeWarning: “Keep source resolution” is selected, so nothing is upscaled. Set a larger output resolution on the “Quality” tab.
rtx.alphaWarning: When keeping alpha, this runs at only about a third of Lanczos's speed, and the alpha channel itself is still upscaled with Lanczos.
rtx.vulkanWarning: No usable Vulkan was detected, so ArtCNN cannot run. Update the graphics driver and detect again.
rtx.vsrHint: NVIDIA RTX super resolution; works only with the NVEncC encoder. The output size is set by the scale below.
rtx.artcnnHint: 2× AI upscaling with crisper lines that keeps the original grain; needs a Vulkan-capable GPU. Set the output size on the “Quality” tab; AI is used only when both width and height grow by more than 1.3×.
rtx.lanczosHint: Fastest, slightly soft. Set the output size on the “Quality” tab.
rtx.artcnnModelHint: C4F32 is about 30%–40% slower with little visible difference.
rtx.qualityHint: For upscaling MMD footage choose 4. 8–19 keep the original size (set scale to 1); strength needs VFX SDK 1.3+.
rtx.vfgHint: Needs an RTX 40 / 50 series GPU, NVEncC 9.36+ and the NVIDIA VFX runtime; alpha is not supported.
rtx.modelDirectoryHint: Leave empty to use NVEncC's bundled model; choose one only if verification reports the model is missing.
rtx.checkHint: RTX VSR / VFG must first run once on this computer with the current settings; encoding is allowed after it passes.
